key_insight: Reliable protein–ligand binding prediction requires trustworthy evaluation, not just strong benchmark scores. The authors advocate transparent data, code and experimental procedures to support fair, reproducible comparisons.
problem_solved: Data leakage, biased evaluation and insufficiently documented experiments can distort performance estimates and make scoring methods difficult to compare meaningfully.
method: Promote transparent reporting and sharing of evaluation data, code and experimental procedures.
Discuss good practices for preventing data leakage and reducing evaluation bias.
Encourage fair, reproducible comparisons across structure-based protein–ligand scoring methods.
impact: These guidelines help AI/ML practitioners assess whether reported improvements are credible and comparable. More rigorous evaluation can support better-informed choices of methods for drug-discovery research.
visual_elements: Protein–ligand binding illustration showing a molecule fitting into a protein pocket.
Train–test split diagram highlighting data leakage and its prevention.
Transparency checklist with icons for data, code and experimental procedures.
Balanced-scale graphic representing fair comparison across scoring methods.
paper_title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction
